title: Untangling Hate Speech Definitions: A Semantic Componential Analysis Across Cultures and Domains
benchmark_measurement: The study's framework, Semantic Componential Analysis (SCA), measures the presence of 'religion' as a fundamental component in 493 hate speech definitions collected from various domains (law, Wikipedia, research papers, etc.) and cultures. The experimental part evaluates how different hate speech definitions, which vary in their inclusion of religious targets, affect the classification performance of Large Language Models.
findings: Religion was identified as the most frequent semantic component across all 493 hate speech definitions analyzed. Its presence as a protected characteristic varied significantly across cultures and domains, such as in the case study of legal definitions in the Levant region (Israel, Syria, Jordan). This variation in definitions, including those pertaining to religion, was shown to impact LLM performance on hate speech detection tasks. The framework also explicitly lists 'Anti-Semitism' as a form of hate.
